previous_disclosures.summary: The market for NVIDIA's products is intensely competitive, characterized by rapid technological change, with principal competitive factors including performance, product breadth, software support, and pricing.

NVIDIA believes its competitiveness depends on anticipating customer demands, delivering consistent volumes at acceptable quality and prices, and expects increased competition from existing and new entrants offering lower prices or better performance.
It is possible that new competitors or alliances among competitors could emerge and acquire significant market share, and some competitors may have greater resources to adapt to changes.

A significant source of competition comes from companies providing GPUs, CPUs, DPUs, embedded SoCs, and other accelerated, AI computing processor products, as well as providers of semiconductor-based high-performance interconnect products.
NVIDIA expects an increasingly competitive environment in the future.

current_disclosures.summary: The market for NVIDIA's products is intensely competitive, characterized by rapid technological change, where key competitive factors include performance, product breadth, software support, and pricing. The company expects competition to increase from both existing players and new entrants offering lower-priced or superior products, with potential for new alliances to acquire significant market share.

Competition stems from companies providing GPUs, CPUs, DPUs, and other accelerated AI computing processors, as well as providers of high-performance interconnect products. Some competitors may possess greater marketing, financial, distribution, and manufacturing resources, enabling them to adapt more quickly to customer or technological changes, leading to an increasingly competitive environment.

NVIDIA identifies several categories of competitors: suppliers of GPUs and accelerated computing solutions (e.g., AMD, Huawei, Intel); large cloud services companies designing internal hardware/software (e.g., Amazon, Microsoft); Arm-based CPU suppliers (e.g., Amazon, Huawei, Microsoft); SoC suppliers for servers and embedded devices (e.g., Ambarella, Broadcom, Qualcomm, Samsung); and networking product suppliers including switches and DPUs (e.g., AMD, Arista, Broadcom, Cisco, Huawei, Intel).

comparisons.peer_topic: Competitive landscape and determinants of product competitiveness
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD operates in a highly competitive market where timely delivery of latest products is critical for revenue growth. Key factors determining product competitiveness include total cost of ownership, performance, features (including AI accelerations), energy efficiency, and software compatibility.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and AMD define the competitive landscape as intense and driven by rapid technological change, but they differ in their specific cited competitive factors. NVIDIA emphasizes software support, API conformity, and manufacturing capabilities as principal factors, whereas AMD places heavier weight on total cost of ownership, energy efficiency, and the timely introduction of products with AI acceleration features. Both companies recognize that performance and product breadth are key determinants of competitiveness.

sentences.text: The market for our products is intensely competitive and is characterized by rapid technological change and evolving industry standards.

We believe that the principal competitive factors in this market are performance, breadth of product offerings, access to customers and partners and distribution channels, software support, conformity to industry standard APIs, manufacturing capabilities, processor pricing, and total system costs.
The markets in which our products are sold are highly competitive and delivering the latest and best products to market on a timely basis is critical to achieving revenue growth.

We believe that the main factors that determine our product competitiveness are total cost of ownership, timely product introductions, product quality, product features and capabilities (including accelerations for key workloads such as AI), energy efficiency (including power consumption and battery life, given their impact on total cost of ownership), reliability, performance, size (or form factor), selling price, cost, adherence to industry standards (and the creation of open industry standards), level of integration, software and hardware compatibility, ease of use and functionality of software design tools, completeness of applicable software solutions, security and stability, brand recognition and availability.

comparisons.peer_summary: AMD expects competition to remain intense due to rapid technological changes and competitors introducing products with better performance or features that could render AMD's products less competitive.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies explicitly expect competition to increase or remain intense due to rapid technological changes and the introduction of superior products by competitors. NVIDIA anticipates increased competition from new entrants offering lower prices or better performance, while AMD expects competitors to introduce products that provide better performance or additional features that could render AMD's products less competitive. Both view the threat of product obsolescence and feature superiority from rivals as a primary competitive risk.

sentences.text: We believe that our ability to remain competitive will depend on how well we are able to anticipate the features and functions that customers and partners will demand and whether we are able to deliver consistent volumes of our products at acceptable levels of quality and at competitive prices.

We expect competition to increase from both existing competitors and new market entrants with products that may be lower priced than ours or may provide better performance or additional features not provided by our products.

We expect that competition will continue to be intense due to rapid technological changes, frequent product introductions by our competitors or new competitors of products that may provide better performance or experiences or that may include additional features that render our products comparatively less competitive.

comparisons.peer_summary: Broadcom operates in highly competitive markets where a consolidation trend is expected to continue, alongside increasing competition from existing competitors expanding offerings and new market entrants. Effectiveness depends on factors such as quality, price, innovation, and customer support.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and Broadcom describe their markets as highly competitive with increasing competition from existing players expanding offerings and new entrants. Broadcom explicitly cites a trend toward consolidation and collaboration among competitors, a factor not mentioned by NVIDIA. While both identify quality, price, and product features as competitive factors, Broadcom includes system-level design capability and engineering expertise, whereas NVIDIA highlights software support, API conformity, and manufacturing capabilities.

Additionally, our ability to compete effectively depends on a number of factors, including: quality, technical performance, price, product features, product system compatibility, system-level design capability, engineering expertise, responsiveness to customers, new product innovation, product availability, delivery timing and reliability, and customer sales and technical support.
